items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: He was a student actually of the late and great T-Bone Walker... But this guy could play, and he was in my seven piece band that I had in later years

ctx.x: Jimmy Ryan's? A lot of guys used to stand on the corner, they tell me, with a saxophone, the guy say, 'Oh, you're a saxophone player. I want a trumpet player.' 'Well, wait a minute, I live right upstairs, let me -- I play trumpet too, you know.' The guys would go get those things, you know. I remember the guys out of Fletcher's band would tell me these things, you know? And I remember them, sure

enough. I used to go down and stand down and watch these things. They said, you want to see guys go upstairs and come out with -- guys used to stand on the street sometime with a trumpet, saxophone, and fiddle. Violin, you know. (Inaudible) Waitin' for -- all gigs in New York. (unintelligible). Then you go to the Metropole, and you know the story of the Metropole. But getting back to a mixed group. We had quite a few fellas that would frequent Minton's, and I used to use a lot of mixed guys, a lot of them -- I…

I would mention that was in that seven piece group -- we're talking in the forties now -- was a trumpet player who was with me for 18 years, even in my Chicago band, and he just died recently -- Gayle Brockman was his name. I'll tell you. I know you'll know him. He's the guy that played the original trumpet solo with Jug. Jug is Gene Ammonds.
